knowledge_point.title: Expressing a Line Integral as a Double Integral Using Green's Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Consider the path $C,$ in the plane, as the boundary of the region enclosed by the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1,$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ According to Green's theorem, 

$$
{∮}_{C}{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡2y\,dx+{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y\,dy={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $C$ is traversed counterclockwise. Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/c4/c44b320dd7ba2824ae0024a3d77d0c6cd6e06fa5889e23879f3d6f464c3a80df.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡2y$ and $Q(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-2{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡2y\,dx+{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y-(-2{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y)]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}({e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y+2{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)=3{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡2y.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the rectangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(0,0),(2,0),(2,1)$ and $(0,1),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ According to Green's theorem, 

$$
{∮}_{C}(y\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2}y)\,dx+(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,dy={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/8d/8d57fb7f6b8e2e822a11f11a0267994c449c37b43df167a8d48ab8036854b8dd.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=y\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2}y$ and $Q(x,y)=x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡y-{x}^{2},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(y\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2}y)\,dx+(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡y-(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡y-{x}^{2})]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-y\operatorname{cos}⁡y+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)={x}^{2}.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the quadrilateral $C$ in the plane with vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(1,1)$ and $(0,2),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ According to Green's theorem, 

$$
{∮}_{C}{y}^{2}{e}^{xy}\,dx+2xy{e}^{xy}\,dy={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/b7/b7fad52bdf54c0870ad4c4939a314f5657e390b589faf76e60a8d8ef5d926039.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={y}^{2}{e}^{xy}$ and $Q(x,y)=2xy{e}^{xy}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=(2y+x{y}^{2}){e}^{xy},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=(2y+2x{y}^{2}){e}^{xy}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}{y}^{2}{e}^{xy}\,dx+2xy{e}^{xy}\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[(2y+2x{y}^{2}){e}^{xy}-(2y+x{y}^{2}){e}^{xy}]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2y+2x{y}^{2}-2y-x{y}^{2}){e}^{xy}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}x{y}^{2}{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)=x{y}^{2}{e}^{xy}.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the rectangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(0,1),(0,-1),(1,-1)$ and $(1,1),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ According to Green's theorem, 

$$
{∮}_{C}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,dx-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\,dy={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/a3/a3e81cfacc47dfa241a5fea64de84e375a58a6d86ceab82c86303763d5e41fe5.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy).$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-2y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,dx-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-(-2y)]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2y(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)=2y(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)).$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the triangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(-1,0),(0,-1)$ and $(1,1),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ According to Green's theorem, 

$$
{∮}_{C}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2xy)\,dx+2{sin}^{2}⁡(xy)\,dy={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/f4/f4bb6636c104cf17bcd4b25037a3490ba30b7c1380b152c33504d9015903bdca.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2xy)$ and $Q(x,y)=2{sin}^{2}⁡xy.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy),\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=4y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)=2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2xy)\,dx+2{sin}^{2}⁡(xy)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy)-(-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy)))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy)+2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2(x+y)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy)\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)=2(x+y)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy).$

knowledge_point.title: Expressing a Line Integral as a Double Integral Using Green's Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Consider the path $C,$ in the plane, as the boundary of the region enclosed by the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1$ and the $x$-axis, for $y\ge 0,$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ According to Green's theorem, 

$$
{∮}_{C}x{e}^{-{y}^{2}}\,dx+{x}^{2}y{e}^{-{y}^{2}}\,dy={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/a0/a0d50e8f2faf679e6dee1471c8fa1ca2be4194796e606fc3e89372f0fefe8cfc.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=x{e}^{-{y}^{2}}$ and $Q(x,y)={x}^{2}y{e}^{-{y}^{2}}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-2xy{e}^{-{y}^{2}},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=2xy{e}^{-{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}x{e}^{-{y}^{2}}\,dx+{x}^{2}y{e}^{-{y}^{2}}\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[2xy{e}^{-{y}^{2}}-(-2xy{e}^{-{y}^{2}})]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2xy{e}^{-{y}^{2}}+2xy{e}^{-{y}^{2}})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}4xy{e}^{-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)=4xy{e}^{-{y}^{2}}.$
